entry.title: Nodejs Daily Email Sending with Third-Party Scheduling and Idempotent Retries
entry.summary: For a daily support report or a renewal reminder, use a scheduling service to trigger a small public HTTP handler and let an email provider deliver the message. Keep the business deadline in the payload, and make the handler idempotent before you add retries. That split leaves scheduling, retry delivery, and email deliverability outside the application process without turning the deadline rule into an invisible cron job. The important design choice is not “which cron syntax?” It is what happens when the scheduler retries after a timeout. A reminder must not be sent twice because the first request reached the email provider and the response disappeared. entry.title: Following Claude Code from a phone without touching the account
entry.summary: Anyone who follows a coding agent from a phone eventually asks the same question: will this put my account at risk? Kiteline, an app for following coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and a dozen others) from an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch, answers with three boundaries. It does not read or store Claude account credentials, does not log in on the user's behalf, and does not call Anthropic's API directly. It only reads the session records Claude Code writes locally and uses the extension points and terminal that Claude Code exposes. The phone talks to the user's own computer (directly on a LAN, otherwise peer-to-peer or through a relay). From Claude's side nothing changes: same machine, same network environment, no new device. An optional feature runs Claude Code in the background on a remote machine so VS Code does not need to stay open. It is off by default and enabled per device; the exit IP is checked and shown before enabling; and the background process must use the same proxy, certificates and API endpoint as Claude Code inside VS Code. If those cannot be read, it falls back to VS Code and says why. Keep one machine and one network exit, do not share an account, do not hand credentials to third-party tools, and use the phone as a remote control only. Claude Code is Anthropic's product; Kiteline is an independent third-party tool. The desktop side is open source on GitHub; the phone app is iOS/iPadOS only (no Android).
